summary: Three promising public sources complement the existing hospital quality and unplanned-visit inputs: CMS post-acute care utilization files for historical provider-level context, New Jersey’s Medicaid transportation instructions for transport eligibility and lead-time workflow, and the state’s NJ FamilyCare health-plan roster for Middlesex County coverage context. The inspected sources do not establish current partner capacity, appointment availability, placement acceptance, or facility-level discharge wait times. Treat records as candidate research requiring independent verification and acquisition.

sources.title: Medicare Post-Acute Care Utilization and Hospice Public Use Files
sources.geography: Provider, state, and national levels; provider records can be filtered to New Jersey and Middlesex County communities. The files describe where a provider is located, not the hospital that referred a patient.
sources.period: CMS’s redesigned PAC pages describe calendar-year data for home health and fiscal-year data for hospice, SNF, IRF, and LTCH. Confirm each dataset’s available years and release version before acquisition; the inspected 2022 methodology documents CY/FY 2013–2020 and should not be used to assert the current page’s coverage.
sources.grain: Provider × service setting × year, with additional state and national summary rows. Historical utilization, not referral-stage or live capacity data.
useful_fields: Provider CCN, name, city, state, ZIP
Charges, allowed amount, Medicare payment and standardized payment
Selected beneficiary demographic, clinical, and discharge-status summaries where present
observed_facts: CMS describes files for home health, hospice, skilled nursing facilities, inpatient rehabilitation facilities, and long-term care hospitals, with provider, state, and national summaries.

CMS’s methodology says the older PAC PUF covers provider-level Medicare fee-for-service utilization and payment summaries; its population excludes Medicare Advantage beneficiaries without a paid fee-for-service claim.
The older methodology cautions that provider cells may be suppressed and that provider-level counts do not necessarily sum to aggregate totals.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Open the CMS PAC catalog, select the current HHA, SNF, IRF, LTCH, and hospice datasets relevant to post-discharge pathways, and record each dataset’s exact release year, downloadable resource URL or documented API/query link, field dictionary, and suppression rules. Filter provider listings to New Jersey and candidate Middlesex-area facilities; crosswalk CCNs to the existing provider inventory. Do not infer New Brunswick hospital referrals or present service counts as available slots.
limitations: The inspected catalog page did not expose a direct file or API URL in the page text, so none is asserted here.
Provider geography is not patient residence or referral origin; service counts are historical utilization, not capacity.
Medicare fee-for-service summaries may not represent NJ FamilyCare, commercial, or Medicare Advantage populations.
No record-level discharge destination or referral-stage acceptance outcome is established by this catalog description.
Access is public according to the CMS catalog description; a specific redistribution license was not verified in the inspected material.

sources.title: Transportation
sources.publisher: New Jersey Division of Medical Assistance and Health Services
sources.geography: Statewide NJ FamilyCare Medicaid transportation benefit; applicable to eligible members in Middlesex County, including New Brunswick, subject to individual eligibility and covered-service rules.
sources.period: Current page inspected 2026-10-10; no historical series or publication date stated on the page.
sources.grain: Program rules and booking workflow, not a quantitative trip dataset.
useful_fields: Eligibility framing: NJ FamilyCare member and medically necessary covered service
Trip request timing: call two days before appointment; phone booking up to one month ahead; online booking advance limit not specified
Required booking information: member ID, pickup address/ZIP, provider identity/address, appointment time/date, special transport needs
Facility discharge and standing-order contact route
observed_facts: The state identifies Modivcare as the transportation broker for NJ FamilyCare clients statewide.
The page says passengers should call two days before an appointment and provides a healthcare-facility line for standing orders and hospital discharges.
These are stated program instructions, not observed wait times or guaranteed dispatch times.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Capture the public state page with retrieval date and source hash; encode only the stated eligibility and booking steps as scenario rules. For each simulated case, represent payer/eligibility, notice time, destination, and special transport needs as inputs; do not convert the stated two-day recommendation into a measured trip duration or assume a ride is available.
limitations: No public quantitative trip-level, denial, dispatch-time, vehicle, or capacity data was found in the inspected page.
The program is specific to eligible NJ FamilyCare members and medically necessary covered services; it does not describe other payers.
Contact details are operational routing information and can change; recheck before use.
The state page’s publication or effective date and a specific data redistribution license were not verified.

sources.title: NJ FamilyCare Health Plans
sources.publisher: New Jersey Division of Medical Assistance and Health Services
sources.geography: New Jersey managed care plans; the page’s plan roster lists Middlesex County among counties served by multiple plans.
sources.period: Current roster inspected 2026-10-10; no historical series or effective date was visible in the inspected page text.
sources.grain: Plan × service-area county, with plan contact information and links to member materials.
useful_fields: Member and provider service contact information
Links to member handbooks, MLTSS supplements, and quick reference guides
observed_facts: The state page lists several contracted NJ FamilyCare plans and includes Middlesex County in their listed service areas.

The state’s separate provider-resources page says most NJ FamilyCare benefits are delivered through managed care and providers generally need to participate in the member’s contracted plan network; the roster alone does not prove any specific post-acute provider is in-network.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Capture the current state roster and the relevant plan handbook or MLTSS supplement for the simulated payer/eligibility rules. Crosswalk plans with separately verified post-acute provider network evidence before marking a candidate partner as in-network. Keep network membership distinct from referral acceptance or capacity.
limitations: This is plan service-area and contact information, not a provider directory or discharge-partner inventory.
The page does not establish whether a particular SNF, home health agency, hospice, IRF, or LTCH accepts a given patient or has openings.
The roster is mutable; verify current effective dates and plan participation at acquisition time.
A specific redistribution license was not verified in the inspected material.

missing_inputs: No inspected public source established live bed, staffing, home-health caseload, hospice admission, or transport capacity for RWJUH or Saint Peter’s discharge referrals.
No verified local public dataset was identified here for referral attempts, acceptance/denial reasons, time-to-placement, time-to-first-follow-up, or discharge transport completion.
No specific direct downloadable CSV/JSON or API endpoint was exposed in the inspected CMS catalog page; discover and verify the chosen dataset resource before cataloguing it as acquired.
A current, independently verified list of ten Middlesex County post-acute/community service entries remains to be collected; public listings alone would not indicate availability.
simulation_use: Use CMS PAC provider-year counts and service days as historical external baselines for broad service-setting mix only after selecting and recording the exact release, geography, grain, and suppression metadata. Do not convert them into local referral probabilities or current slots. Use the NJ transportation page to define an eligibility-gated booking workflow, including advance-notice and special-needs inputs, while leaving dispatch time and success probability uncalibrated. Use the plan roster to represent payer-network checks and coverage barriers, pending provider-specific network verification. Keep historical readmission outcomes as separate outcome measures rather than direct event probabilities. A draft blocker taxonomy for independent review can include payer/eligibility mismatch; out-of-network partner; clinical/service-scope mismatch; no confirmed placement; missing authorization or referral documentation; patient/family preference or caregiver unavailability; transport eligibility, notice, accessibility, or dispatch barrier; home environment/equipment barrier; and follow-up provider or appointment not confirmed. These are candidate categories, not measured local prevalence.
limitations: Research was bounded to two web searches and four primary-source page opens; no other sources were inspected.
No dataset was downloaded or acquired in this task. Discovery records are not acquisition receipts.

The CMS catalog description was found in search and its catalog page was opened, but the open response exposed no usable page content or direct resource link; exact current dataset versions and download/API URLs remain unverified.
The older CMS methodology provides useful definitions but is not evidence of the current CMS release’s exact fields or years.
This is candidate research for independent verification and domain-owner applicability review, not simulation calibration.
